g.text: An eight-week public-furniture project guided by Dyutiman Moulik, developed from
ergonomic intent through a full-scale mould and spatial visualisation.
Construct outdoor public furniture that is ergonomic, works for all age groups
References focused on open forms, concrete mass, timber warmth and the
relationship between a resting body and a public landscape.
A sun-board scale model established the form. Metal mesh was embedded for
support, then white cement with dyes was poured to preview the intended
The curved geometry was translated into a technical drawing so form,
thickness and construction could be resolved before scaling.
A full-scale CAD print was mapped directly onto the build surface to position
the mould and screw points accurately.
Truss work, reinforcement and mould preparation tested how the sculptural
object could be cast and supported at full scale.
The final form was visualised as part of a public environment—not as an
isolated object—showing space to pause, lounge, read or simply exist.
